sanskrit: kathaṃ tv aham asaṃkliṣṭo gaccheyaṃ paramāṃ gatim nāvarteyaṃ yathā bhūyo yonisaṃsārasāgare
english: How then, untainted, might I reach the supreme goal, so that I never again return into the ocean of birth and transmigration?

sanskrit: paraṃ bhāvaṃ hi kāṅkṣāmi yatra nāvartate punaḥ sarvasaṅgān parityajya niścitāṃ manaso gatim
english: For I long for that highest state from which there is no returning, abandoning all attachments and the resolute course of the mind.

sanskrit: tatra yāsyāmi yatrātmā śamaṃ me 'dhigamiṣyati akṣayaś cāvyayaś caiva yatra sthāsyāmi śāśvataḥ
english: There I shall go, where my self will attain peace, where, imperishable and undecaying, I shall abide everlasting.

sanskrit: na tu yogam ṛte śakyā prāptuṃ sā paramā gatiḥ avabandho hi muktasya karmabhir nopapadyate
english: But that supreme goal cannot be reached without yoga, for no bondage through deeds can befall the one who is liberated.

sanskrit: tasmād yogaṃ samāsthāya tyaktvā gṛhakalevaram vāyubhūtaḥ pravekṣyāmi tejorāśiṃ divākaram
english: Therefore, taking my stand in yoga and casting off this dwelling that is the body, becoming wind itself I shall enter the mass of radiance, the sun, maker of day.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa kṣayam āpnoti somaḥ suragaṇair yathā kampitaḥ patate bhūmiṃ punaś caivādhirohati kṣīyate hi sadā somaḥ punaś caivābhipūryate
english: For this does not meet with the waning that the moon, Soma, suffers among the host of gods: shaken, it falls toward the earth and rises up again, for Soma ever wanes and is filled full once more.

sanskrit: ravis tu saṃtāpayati lokān raśmibhir ulbaṇaiḥ sarvatas teja ādatte nityam akṣayamaṇḍalaḥ
english: The sun, however, scorches the worlds with its fierce rays and draws in radiance from every side, its orb forever undiminished.

sanskrit: ato me rocate gantum ādityaṃ dīptatejasam atra vatsyāmi durdharṣo niḥsaṅgenāntarātmanā
english: Therefore it pleases me to go to the Āditya of blazing splendor; there I shall dwell, unassailable, with an inner self free of all attachment.

sanskrit: sūryasya sadane cāhaṃ nikṣipyedaṃ kalevaram ṛṣibhiḥ saha yāsyāmi sauraṃ tejo 'tiduḥsaham
english: And in the abode of Sūrya I shall lay down this body and, together with the seers, pass into the solar radiance that none can scarcely bear.

sanskrit: āpṛcchāmi nagān nāgān girīn urvīṃ diśo divam devadānavagandharvān piśācoragarākṣasān
english: I take my leave of the trees and the serpents, of the mountains, the earth, the quarters and the sky, of the gods, the Dānavas and Gandharvas, of Piśācas, Uragas, and Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: lokeṣu sarvabhūtāni pravekṣyāmi nasaṃśayaḥ paśyantu yogavīryaṃ me sarve devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ
english: Free of doubt, I shall enter into all beings throughout the worlds; let all the gods, together with the seers, behold the power of my yoga.

sanskrit: athānujñāpya tam ṛṣiṃ nāradaṃ lokaviśrutam tasmād anujñāṃ saṃprāpya jagāma pitaraṃ prati
english: Then, asking leave of that seer Nārada, renowned throughout the worlds, and having received his leave, he went toward his father.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya mahātmānam ṛṣiṃ dvaipāyanaṃ munim śukaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya kṛṣṇam āpṛṣṭavān muniḥ
english: Saluting the great-souled seer, the sage Dvaipāyana, and circling Kṛṣṇa reverently, the sage Śuka took his leave of him.

sanskrit: śrutvā ṛṣis tad vacanaṃ śukasya; prīto mahātmā punar āha cainam bho bhoḥ putra sthīyatāṃ tāvad adya; yāvac cakṣuḥ prīṇayāmi tvadartham
english: Hearing those words of Śuka, the great-souled seer, well pleased, spoke to him once more: "O my son, my son, stay yet this one day, so that I may gladden my eyes for your sake."

sanskrit: nirapekṣaḥ śuko bhūtvā niḥsneho muktabandhanaḥ mokṣam evānusaṃcintya gamanāya mano dadhe pitaraṃ saṃparityajya jagāma dvijasattamaḥ
english: But Śuka, become indifferent, free of affection, his bonds undone, fixing his thought on liberation alone, set his mind on departure; and that best of the twice-born, taking leave of his father, went his way.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca giripṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya suto vyāsasya bhārata same deśe vivikte ca niḥśalāka upāviśat
english: Bhīṣma said: Ascending the mountain's ridge, O descendant of Bharata, the son of Vyāsa sat down in a level and secluded spot, wholly free of thorns and distractions.

sanskrit: dhārayām āsa cātmānaṃ yathāśāstraṃ mahāmuniḥ pādāt prabhṛtigātreṣu krameṇa kramayogavit
english: And that great sage, skilled in the graded discipline, held his self in restraint according to the scriptures, fixing it limb by limb, beginning from the feet, in due order.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa prāṅmukho vidvān āditye nacirodite pāṇipādaṃ samādhāya vinītavad upāviśat
english: Then the learned one, facing east while the sun had risen but a little while, composing hands and feet, sat down with humble bearing.

sanskrit: na tatra pakṣisaṃghāto na śabdo nāpi darśanam yatra vaiyāsakir dhīmān yoktuṃ samupacakrame
english: There where the wise son of Vyāsa set himself to enter into yoga, there was no flock of birds, no sound, and nothing to be seen.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tadātmānaṃ sarvasaṅgaviniḥsṛtam prajahāsa tato hāsaṃ śukaḥ saṃprekṣya bhāskaram
english: He then beheld his own self released from every attachment; and gazing upon the sun, Śuka broke into laughter.

sanskrit: sa punar yogam āsthāya mokṣamārgopalabdhaye mahāyogīśvaro bhūtvā so 'tyakrāmad vihāyasam
english: Again taking his stand in yoga to win the path of liberation, and becoming a great lord of yogins, he soared up into the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā devarṣiṃ nāradaṃ tadā nivedayām āsa tadā svaṃ yogaṃ paramarṣaye
english: Then, circling reverently the divine seer Nārada, he made known his yoga to that supreme seer.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭo mārgaḥ pravṛtto 'smi svasti te 'stu tapodhana tvatprasādād gamiṣyāmi gatim iṣṭāṃ mahādyute
english: "The path is seen, and I have set forth. May it be well with you, O treasury of austerity. By your grace I shall go, O greatly resplendent one, to the goal I desire."

sanskrit: nāradenābhyanujñātas tato dvaipāyanātmajaḥ abhivādya punar yogam āsthāyākāśam āviśat
english: Granted leave by Nārada, the son of Dvaipāyana then, saluting him, took his stand once more in yoga and entered the sky.

sanskrit: kailāsapṛṣṭhād utpatya sa papāta divaṃ tadā antarikṣacaraḥ śrīmān vyāsaputraḥ suniścitaḥ
english: Springing up from the ridge of Kailāsa, he then flew into the heavens, the glorious son of Vyāsa, mover through the firmament, wholly resolved.

sanskrit: tam udyantaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ vainateyasamadyutim dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni manomārutaraṃhasam
english: As that best of the twice-born rose up, splendid as the son of Vinatā and swift as mind and wind, all beings beheld him.

sanskrit: vyavasāyena lokāṃs trīn sarvān so 'tha vicintayan āsthito divyam adhvānaṃ pāvakārkasamaprabhaḥ
english: By his resolve contemplating all the three worlds entire, he held to the divine course, his radiance equal to fire and sun.

sanskrit: tam ekamanasaṃ yāntam avyagram akutobhayam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni jaṅgamānītarāṇi ca
english: All beings, both the moving and the unmoving, beheld him as he went, single of mind, untroubled, and fearing nothing from any quarter.

sanskrit: yathāśakti yathānyāyaṃ pūjayāṃ cakrire tadā puṣpavarṣaiś ca divyais tam avacakrur divaukasaḥ
english: Then, each as best they could and as was fitting, they worshipped him; and the dwellers of heaven covered him with showers of divine flowers.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ sarve gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ṛṣayaś caiva saṃsiddhāḥ paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ
english: Beholding him, all the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases were amazed, and the seers who had attained perfection fell into utter wonder.

sanskrit: antarikṣacaraḥ ko 'yaṃ tapasā siddhim āgataḥ adhaḥkāyordhvavaktraś ca netraiḥ samabhivāhyate
english: "Who is this that travels the firmament, come to perfection through austerity, his body downward and his face turned up, borne onward by the eyes of all?"

sanskrit: tataḥ paramadhīrātmā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ bhāskaraṃ samudīkṣan sa prāṅmukho vāgyato 'gamat śabdenākāśam akhilaṃ pūrayann iva sarvataḥ
english: Then that supremely steadfast one, renowned throughout the three worlds, gazing upon the sun, went onward facing east with speech restrained, as though filling the whole of space with sound on every side.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā dṛṣṭvā sarvāpsarogaṇāḥ saṃbhrāntamanaso rājann āsan paramavismitāḥ pañcacūḍāprabhṛtayo bhṛśam utphullalocanāḥ
english: Seeing him suddenly approaching, all the hosts of Apsarases, O king, were bewildered in mind and seized with the greatest wonder—Pañcacūḍā and the rest, their eyes opened wide.

sanskrit: daivataṃ katamaṃ hy etad uttamāṃ gatim āsthitam suniścitam ihāyāti vimuktam iva niḥspṛham
english: "Which deity is this, set upon the highest goal, who comes here so wholly resolved, like one liberated and without desire?"

sanskrit: tataḥ samaticakrāma malayaṃ nāma parvatam urvaśī pūrvacittiś ca yaṃ nityam upasevate te sma brahmarṣiputrasya vismayaṃ yayatuḥ param
english: Then he passed beyond the mountain named Malaya, which Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti ever frequent; and they came to the utmost wonder at the son of the brahman-seer.

sanskrit: aho buddhisamādhānaṃ vedābhyāsarate dvije acireṇaiva kālena nabhaś carati candravat pitṛśuśrūṣayā siddhiṃ saṃprāpto 'yam anuttamām
english: "Ah, the steadiness of mind in this brahman devoted to the study of the Vedas! In so short a time he ranges the sky like the moon. Through obedient service to his father he has attained perfection beyond compare."

sanskrit: pitṛbhakto dṛḍhatapāḥ pituḥ sudayitaḥ sutaḥ ananyamanasā tena kathaṃ pitrā vivarjitaḥ
english: "Devoted to his father, firm in austerity, a son most dear to his father—how was he forsaken by that father whose mind was set on nothing else?"

sanskrit: urvaśyā vacanaṃ śrutvā śukaḥ paramadharmavit udaikṣata diśaḥ sarvā vacane gatamānasaḥ
english: Hearing the words of Urvaśī, Śuka, supreme knower of dharma, looked out upon all the quarters, his mind intent upon their speech.

sanskrit: so 'ntarikṣaṃ mahīṃ caiva saśailavanakānanām ālokayām āsa tadā sarāṃsi saritas tathā
english: He gazed then upon the firmament and the earth with its mountains, woods, and forests, and likewise upon the lakes and the rivers.

sanskrit: tato dvaipāyanasutaṃ bahumānapuraḥsaram kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarvā nirīkṣante sma devatāḥ
english: Then all the deities, their palms joined in reverence, gazed upon the son of Dvaipāyana with the highest honor.

sanskrit: abravīt tās tadā vākyaṃ śukaḥ paramadharmavit pitā yady anugacchen māṃ krośamānaḥ śuketi vai
english: Then Śuka, supreme knower of dharma, spoke these words to them: "If my father should come after me, crying out 'Śuka! Śuka!'—

sanskrit: tataḥ prativaco deyaṃ sarvair eva samāhitaiḥ etan me snehataḥ sarve vacanaṃ kartum arhatha
english: "then an answer should be given by all of you, with one accord. Out of affection for me, may you all see fit to do as I say."

sanskrit: śukasya vacanaṃ śrutvā diśaḥ savanakānanāḥ samudrāḥ saritaḥ śailāḥ pratyūcus taṃ samantataḥ
english: Hearing the words of Śuka, the quarters with their groves and forests, the oceans, the rivers, and the mountains answered him from every side:

sanskrit: yathājñāpayase vipra bāḍham evaṃ bhaviṣyati ṛṣer vyāharato vākyaṃ prativakṣyāmahe vayam
english: "As you command, O brahman, so verily shall it be. When the seer utters his words, we shall make answer."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ brahmarṣiḥ sumahātapāḥ prātiṣṭhata śukaḥ siddhiṃ hitvā lokāṃś caturvidhān
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken these words, the brahman-seer Śuka of mighty austerity set forth to perfection, leaving behind the fourfold worlds.

sanskrit: tamo hy aṣṭavidhaṃ hitvā jahau pañcavidhaṃ rajaḥ tataḥ sattvaṃ jahau dhīmāṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Casting off the eightfold darkness and forsaking the fivefold passion, the wise one then forsook even goodness; and it was as if a marvel.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin pade nitye nirguṇe liṅgavarjite brahmaṇi pratyatiṣṭhat sa vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Then in that eternal state, free of the qualities and bereft of all mark, in Brahman he stood firm, blazing like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: ulkāpātā diśāṃ dāhā bhūmikampās tathaiva ca prādurbhūtāḥ kṣaṇe tasmiṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Falling meteors, burnings of the quarters, and earthquakes too broke forth in that instant; and it was as if a marvel.

sanskrit: drumāḥ śākhāś ca mumucuḥ śikharāṇi ca parvatāḥ nirghātaśabdaiś ca girir himavān dīryatīva ha
english: The trees let fall their branches and the mountains their peaks, and Himavān, with the sound of thunderclaps, seemed as though it were splitting apart.

sanskrit: na babhāse sahasrāṃśur na jajvāla ca pāvakaḥ hradāś ca saritaś caiva cukṣubhuḥ sāgarās tathā
english: The thousand-rayed sun shone no more, and the fire blazed no more; the pools and the rivers, and the oceans likewise, were thrown into turmoil.

sanskrit: vavarṣa vāsavas toyaṃ rasavac ca sugandhi ca vavau samīraṇaś cāpi divyagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ
english: Vāsava rained down water savory and sweet of scent, and the wind too blew, pure and bearing the fragrance of heaven.

sanskrit: sa śṛṅge 'pratime divye himavan merusaṃbhave saṃśliṣṭe śvetapīte dve rukmarūpyamaye śubhe
english: There were two peerless, divine peaks, born of Himavān and Meru, joined together, the one white and the other golden, made of silver and of gold, both fair—

sanskrit: śatayojanavistāre tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca bhārata udīcīṃ diśam āśritya rucire saṃdadarśa ha
english: a hundred yojanas in breadth, across and upward, O descendant of Bharata; and resting toward the northern quarter, those two resplendent peaks he beheld.

sanskrit: so 'viśaṅkena manasā tathaivābhyapatac chukaḥ tataḥ parvataśṛṅge dve sahasaiva dvidhākṛte adṛśyetāṃ mahārāja tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: With a mind free of all hesitation Śuka flew straight at them; whereupon the two mountain peaks, O great king, all at once appeared cleft in twain; and it was as if a marvel.

sanskrit: tataḥ parvataśṛṅgābhyāṃ sahasaiva viniḥsṛtaḥ na ca pratijaghānāsya sa gatiṃ parvatottamaḥ
english: Then he passed out from between the two mountain peaks all at once, and that best of mountains did not hinder his passage.

sanskrit: tato mahān abhūc chabdo divi sarvadivaukasām gandharvāṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca ye ca śailanivāsinaḥ
english: Then a great cry arose in heaven from all the dwellers of the sky, from the Gandharvas and the seers, and from those who dwell upon the mountains.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śukam atikrāntaṃ parvataṃ ca dvidhākṛtam sādhu sādhv iti tatrāsīn nādaḥ sarvatra bhārata
english: Beholding Śuka passed beyond and the mountain cleft in twain, there arose on every side the cry "Well done! Well done!", O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: sa pūjyamāno devaiś ca gandharvair ṛṣibhis tathā yakṣarākṣasasaṃghaiś ca vidyādharagaṇais tathā
english: He was honored by the gods and the Gandharvas and the seers, and by the hosts of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas and the throngs of Vidyādharas.

sanskrit: divyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ samākīrṇam antarikṣaṃ samantataḥ āsīt kila mahārāja śukābhipatane tadā
english: The firmament was strewn on every side with divine flowers, O great king, at the soaring of Śuka in that hour.

sanskrit: tato mandākinīṃ ramyām upariṣṭād abhivrajan śuko dadarśa dharmātmā puṣpitadrumakānanām
english: Then, passing above the lovely Mandākinī, the righteous Śuka beheld it with its forests of trees in flower.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ krīḍanty abhiratāḥ snānti caivāpsarogaṇāḥ śūnyākāraṃ nirākārāḥ śukaṃ dṛṣṭvā vivāsasaḥ
english: In its waters the hosts of Apsarases sport with delight and bathe; unclothed, and themselves heedless of form, they beheld Śuka who was empty of all form.

sanskrit: taṃ prakramantam ājñāya pitā snehasamanvitaḥ uttamāṃ gatim āsthāya pṛṣṭhato 'nusasāra ha
english: Aware that he was departing, his father, filled with affection, took to the highest course and followed after him from behind.

sanskrit: śukas tu mārutād ūrdhvaṃ gatiṃ kṛtvāntarikṣagām darśayitvā prabhāvaṃ svaṃ sarvabhūto 'bhavat tadā
english: But Śuka, having made his course through the firmament swifter than the wind and shown forth his own power, then became one with all beings.

sanskrit: mahāyogagatiṃ tv agryāṃ vyāsotthāya mahātapāḥ nimeṣāntaramātreṇa śukābhipatanaṃ yayau
english: And Vyāsa of great austerity, rising up by the foremost course of mighty yoga, in the mere space between two blinks went after Śuka's flight.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa dvidhā kṛtvā parvatāgraṃ śukaṃ gatam śaśaṃsur ṛṣayas tasmai karma putrasya tat tadā
english: He beheld where Śuka had passed, having cleft the mountain's summit in twain; and the seers then recounted to him that deed of his son.

sanskrit: tataḥ śuketi dīrgheṇa śaikṣeṇākranditas tadā svayaṃ pitrā svareṇoccais trīṃl lokān anunādya vai
english: Then "Śuka!" with a long and trained call was the cry his father himself raised aloud, his voice resounding through the three worlds.

sanskrit: śukaḥ sarvagato bhūtvā sarvātmā sarvatomukhaḥ pratyabhāṣata dharmātmā bhoḥśabdenānunādayan
english: Śuka, become all-pervading, the self of all, facing every way, the righteous one answered back, making all resound with the sound "Bhoḥ!"

sanskrit: tata ekākṣaraṃ nādaṃ bho ity eva samīrayan pratyāharaj jagat sarvam uccaiḥ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: Then, sounding forth the single-syllabled cry "Bhoḥ!", the whole world, moving and unmoving, gave it back aloud.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti cādyāpi śabdān uccāritān pṛthak girigahvarapṛṣṭheṣu vyājahāra śukaṃ prati
english: And from that time even to this day, in the caverns and ridges of the mountains, sounds severally uttered have echoed back in answer to "Śuka."

sanskrit: antarhitaḥ prabhāvaṃ tu darśayitvā śukas tadā guṇān saṃtyajya śabdādīn padam adhyagamat param
english: But having shown forth his power, Śuka then vanished from sight, and forsaking the qualities, sound and the rest, he attained the supreme state.

sanskrit: mahimānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā putrasyāmitatejasaḥ niṣasāda giriprasthe putram evānucintayan
english: But beholding that greatness of his son of boundless splendor, he sat down upon the mountain's tableland, brooding upon his son alone.

sanskrit: tato mandākinītīre krīḍanto 'psarasāṃ gaṇāḥ āsādya tam ṛṣiṃ sarvāḥ saṃbhrāntā gatacetasaḥ
english: Then the hosts of Apsarases, sporting on the bank of the Mandākinī, all came upon that seer and were bewildered, their senses fled.

sanskrit: jale nililyire kāś cit kāś cid gulmān prapedire vasanāny ādaduḥ kāś cid dṛṣṭvā taṃ munisattamam
english: Some hid themselves in the water, some took refuge in the thickets, and some, beholding that best of sages, snatched up their garments.

sanskrit: tāṃ muktatāṃ tu vijñāya muniḥ putrasya vai tadā saktatām ātmanaś caiva prīto 'bhūd vrīḍitaś ca ha
english: But the sage, perceiving that liberation of his son and his own attachment, was at once gladdened and ashamed.

sanskrit: taṃ devagandharvavṛto maharṣigaṇapūjitaḥ pinākahasto bhagavān abhyāgacchata śaṃkaraḥ
english: To him, surrounded by gods and Gandharvas and honored by the hosts of great seers, came the blessed Śaṃkara, the Pināka in his hand.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahādevaḥ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ tadā
english: To Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, then scorched with grief for his son, Mahādeva spoke these words, with consolation foremost:

sanskrit: agner bhūmer apāṃ vāyor antarikṣasya caiva ha vīryeṇa sadṛśaḥ putras tvayā mattaḥ purā vṛtaḥ
english: "A son equal in power to fire, to earth, to the waters, to wind, and to the firmament itself you once asked of me long ago.

sanskrit: sa tathālakṣaṇo jātas tapasā tava saṃbhṛtaḥ mama caiva prabhāvena brahmatejomayaḥ śuciḥ
english: "Such, marked with those very signs, was the son born to you, nurtured by your austerity and by my power—pure, made wholly of the splendor of Brahman.

sanskrit: sa gatiṃ paramāṃ prāpto duṣprāpām ajitendriyaiḥ daivatair api viprarṣe taṃ tvaṃ kim anuśocasi
english: "He has attained the supreme goal, hard to win even for the gods whose senses are unconquered, O brahman-seer. Why then do you grieve for him?

sanskrit: yāvat sthāsyanti girayo yāvat sthāsyanti sāgarāḥ tāvat tavākṣayā kīrtiḥ saputrasya bhaviṣyati
english: "As long as the mountains shall stand, as long as the oceans shall endure, so long shall your fame, together with your son's, remain imperishable."
